title: Saṅkalpa for the arghya (morning)

words.gram: compound; final member dvāra, n., instr. sg. used adverbially
words.meaning: by way of the destruction of all the faults incurred
words.role: states the means: the rite works by removing faults

words.gram: compound ending in -artham (acc. sg. used adverbially, ‘for the sake of’)
words.meaning: for the pleasure of the glorious Supreme Lord
words.role: states the purpose of the act

words.meaning: the offering of the arghya of the sandhyā

samasa.vigraha: उपात्तानां समस्तानां दुरितानां क्षयः, तेन द्वारेण
samasa.meaning: by way of the destruction of all the faults that have been incurred
for the pleasure of the glorious Supreme Lord
the giving of the arghya (water of honour) of the sandhyā

translation.literal: By way of the destruction of all the faults incurred by me, for the pleasure of the glorious Supreme Lord, I shall perform the giving of the morning sandhyā’s arghya.
translation.readable: To remove every fault I have incurred, and for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord, I shall offer the arghya of the morning Sandhyā.

meaning: The saṅkalpa, the statement of intent, for the arghya, the offering of water to the Sun, in the morning. It names the means — the removal of all the faults one has incurred — and the purpose, the pleasure of the Supreme Lord, and then the act itself. The verbs are first person: the worshipper speaks for himself, and the formula is the same for every performer.
in_the_rite: Morning service, step arghya, before the viniyoga of the arghya and the Gāyatrī.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: A saṅkalpa is said with the breath held after the prāṇāyāma, or immediately after it; it names the act, the time, and the purpose. The Smārta form offers the act for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara); Vaiṣṇava prayogas use other wording, which is outside this edition.
